svg.text: Most serious incidents begin with information that was known, but was never passed on clearly.
SITUATION — who, where, and what is wrong right now
This is Sister Mensah on female ward. Mr Owusu in bed 6 has become breathless in the last hour.
BACKGROUND — the context needed to understand it
He is day 3 after laparotomy, has known heart failure, and had 2 units transfused this morning.
ASSESSMENT — the numbers, and what you think is happening
Respiration 32, saturation 88 per cent in air, pulse 118, crackles at both bases. I think he is overloaded.
RECOMMENDATION — say what you want, and by when
Please review him within ten minutes. May I start oxygen and sit him upright while I wait?
The R is the part most often left out — and it is the part that gets the patient seen.
Never end a handover with only a description. End it with a request and a time.
